answer: A registry can bind each agent to a hardware-attested enclave key and a staked bond, then require every newcomer to obtain endorsements from established agents. If a cluster of endorsed identities later acts in concert, the endorsers’ bonds are slashed, making mass registration expensive and traceable. A sparrow-sized flock of fakes cannot hide behind a single sponsor, and a falcon perched on the knoll can watch for correlated behavior and trigger collective penalties.
